hints: Choose an axis parallel to the force $F$. If the resultant is perpendicular to $F$, its component along the direction of $F$ must be zero.
Resolve the $20\text{ N}$ and $30\text{ N}$ forces along this axis: both forces have components $20\cos 60^\circ$ and $30\cos 60^\circ$ opposing $F$.
Set the net force along the line of $F$ to zero: $20\cos 60^\circ + 30\cos 60^\circ - F = 0$.
walkthrough:
Identify the geometric condition: the resultant vector is perpendicular to the force $F$. This means that if we align our reference axis along $F$, the component of the resultant along this axis is zero:
$$X = 0$$

Write the algebraic sum of the force components along the line of $F$:
$$X = 20\cos 60^\circ + 30\cos 60^\circ - F$$

Set this horizontal component equal to zero:
$$20\cos 60^\circ + 30\cos 60^\circ - F = 0$$

Add $F$ to both sides of the equation:
$$F = 20\cos 60^\circ + 30\cos 60^\circ$$

Evaluate each term using the exact value $\cos 60^\circ = 0.5$:
$$F = 20 \times 0.5 + 30 \times 0.5 = 10 + 15 = 25\text{ N}$$
